# checker.scramble_lines { #puzzle_widget.checker.scramble_lines }

```python
puzzle_widget.checker.scramble_lines(lines, expected, seed=DEFAULT_SEED)
```

Return a shuffled copy of ``lines`` that does not already solve the puzzle.

The lines an author writes are usually in (or near) the correct order,
and a puzzle whose starting order is already solved -- or simply the
order it was written in -- isn't a puzzle. This shuffles them with a
fixed seed, so the scramble is random-looking but deterministic (the
same puzzle always starts the same way), and rejects any candidate that

- equals the order that was passed in, or
- already produces ``expected`` (checked with ``run_puzzle``),

reshuffling until one qualifies.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**lines**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of str]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The puzzle's lines, in any order.

<code>[**expected**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[object](`object`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The target value, used to reject an already-solved shuffle.

<code>[**seed**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [DEFAULT_SEED]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Seed for the shuffle. Defaults to ``DEFAULT_SEED`` (7), so the same puzzle always starts in the same scrambled order.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of str]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   A scrambled order. Degenerate puzzles where no such order exists (fewer than two lines, all lines identical, or every permutation solving the puzzle) fall back to a copy of ``lines`` unchanged -- there is nothing better to show, and raising would be worse than displaying an unscrambled puzzle.
